summary.headline: Rikhav Securities H2 FY26 PAT fell to INR1.20 crore (EPS 0.31) on cash-market investment losses; FY26 PAT INR18.96 crore.
summary.overview: H2 FY26 total income was INR1,604 crore (as stated), EBITDA INR6.57 crore and PAT INR1.20 crore. FY26 total income was INR1,991 crore, EBITDA INR32.53 crore and PAT INR18.96 crore, with EPS of 4.95. Management attributed the weak profit to a loss of roughly INR18-23 crore on legacy cash-market equity investments, valuation losses at the 31 March 2026 market low, higher depreciation from about INR5.40 crore of technology spend, and an unrecognised SLBM profit of INR4.33 crore expected to be realised in coming quarters. Management is cutting cash-market exposure and SME inventory, and is building institutional broking, ETF market making and commodity arbitrage. Several answers were vague or deferred to email, and the call was disrupted by line dropouts.

financial_highlights.change: Expected to realise in coming quarters; management said April in one answer

segments.name: Broking (retail/HNI)
segments.commentary: Brokerage per client is about INR5,000-6,000, with about 50% of revenue from brokerage and float income exceeding brokerage. Management said retail and HNI brokerage has been hard to grow over the last six months.

segments.name: Proprietary trading / algo and arbitrage
segments.commentary: In-house algo and arbitrage were the only area that improved, per management. Algo and delta-hedging income is guided to grow 20-25% in FY27.

segments.name: Market making (SME and ETF)
segments.commentary: SME exposure was cut to about 30% of last year's level, roughly INR20-25 crore. Market making in ETFs has started with Kotak Mutual Fund, with two or three more mutual funds planned.

segments.name: Institutional broking
segments.commentary: Empanelled Kotak Mutual Fund, Bank of India and RBL Bank, and 8-10 FPIs have started. Management said real revenue will start next year and expects SBI and LIC empanelment.

segments.name: Commodities
segments.commentary: Commodity arbitrage and trading started, with gross arbitrage profit of about INR12 crore stated for the period.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: around 20% growth in brokerage and client income, and 20-25% growth in algo trading and delta-hedging income.
Management guided FY27 full-year revenue of around INR40 crore; the basis and line item were not clarified, so treat it as unclear.
Cash-market investments to be cut by INR50 crore, with a further INR50 crore cut planned; total cash-market deployment capped at about INR50 crore in FY27.
Branch and franchise expansion of 10-12 per year at minimum, with cautious rollout. New branches opened in Lucknow, Nashik and Gorakhpur.
Digital marketing to start after the current quarter, once the platform is made seamless.
capex_capacity: About INR5.40 crore spent on computer software and technology enhancement in FY26, which raised depreciation.
Cumulative technology investment over two years is about INR7.5-10 crore.
Technology stack is about 30-40% in-house and about 50% third-party vendors (front office and related systems); spend on servers for low-latency trading and an in-house algo desk.
Backup servers are designed to go live within 5-10 minutes after a front-office hardware failure.
Plans to deploy AI-led audit and analytics in a regulated, human-vetted way; data gathering restricted to institutional clients for now.
demand_pricing: Active client base is about 12,500, with about 2,500 clients added in H1 FY26. Of about 25,000 total customers, about 10,000-12,000 trade quarterly, about 8,000-9,000 are monthly brokerage-generating, and about 2,000-2,500 trade daily.
Retail onboarding is 100% digital (e-KYC via a third-party vendor), with account-opening cost of INR60-70 and overall cost per account of about INR500.
Management said it charges the same brokerage as discount brokers and competes on dealer personal touch.
SEBI derivatives tariff circular: management sees a short-term hit to volumes and a long-term benefit as retail traders shift savings to investing.
Management said the retail and HNI participation recovery depends on a market revival.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the pressure on PAT and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a loss of INR18-20 crore on cash-market shares bought about 1.5 years earlier, unrealised SLBM profit of INR4-4.5 crore, about INR30 lakh more depreciation and INR75-80 lakh of tax adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SME share of inventory and value?
qa_highlights.answer: SME exposure is now about 30% of last year's level, around INR20-25 crore. Management said the whole stock is sold within a week of listing.

qa_highlights.question: Did the ~INR8-10 crore result hit come from valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about INR8-10 crore of the impact to valuation at 31 March, when Nifty was below 23,000 amid the US-Iran conflict.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cumulative technology investment and how is the stack split?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative spend is INR7.5-10 crore over two years. About 30-40% is in-house and about 50% goes to third-party vendors.

qa_highlights.question: Cybersecurity breaches and audits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no attempted breaches or disruptions this year. Trading endpoints get monthly audits, with a third-party listed entity doing reviews.

qa_highlights.question: Client base and ARPU?
qa_highlights.answer: About 12,500 active clients plus 2,500 added in H1. Revenue per user is about INR5,000-6,000, with institutional revenue expected from next year.

qa_highlights.question: Digital CAC and retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital account-opening costs INR60-70 and total cost per account about INR500. No digital marketing has started yet, and relationship-based retention is about 100%.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity and accounting-change questions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stock purchase line changed from investment to trading from October 2024, so the prior-year figures are not comparable. Other queries were deferred to email.

risks_watch: Legacy cash-market equity losses (INR18-23 crore) and valuation exposure remain; the INR50 crore cap on cash-market deployment is a near-term test.
Reliance on algo and arbitrage income, with retail and HNI brokerage stagnant.
Short-term volume hit from the SEBI derivatives tariff circular.
Realisation of the INR4.33 crore SLBM profit, which management said would come in April.
Intake of institutional clients and whether the SBI and LIC empanelments happen.
Disclosure quality: several answers were vague or deferred to email. The stock-in-trade purchase line and the 'other expenses' line were not explained on the call.
Conflicting inputs: the call gave both 'March 2027' and 'FY27' for the INR40 crore figure, and the cumulative technology spend was given as a range.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term structure and technology, but defensive and vague on specifics such as the income jump, stock-in-trade purchases, SME exposure and guidance. Management deferred several questions to email and repeated the market-downturn explanation.
